title: Student police officer charged with rape and kidnap

evidence_packet.title: Student police officer charged with rape and kidnap
evidence_packet.lead: The trainee police officer serving with Greater Manchester Police is charged with multiple offences
evidence_packet.summary: The trainee police officer serving with Greater Manchester Police is charged with multiple offences
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A trainee police officer has been charged with the rape and kidnap of a woman in Manchester Mohammad Hassan, 23, serving with Greater Manchester Police (GMP), has been charged with multiple offences after reports made to the force on Saturday evening which ended in a pursuit on the M62 in West Yorkshire The force previously said a 999 call had been received at about 22:20 BST during which a woman could be heard in a vehicle in the Manchester area Hassan, who has been suspended by the force, has been charged with rape, kidnap, strangulation, sexual assault, theft of a mobile phone and dangerous driving. He is due to appear at Manchester Magistrates' Court later Assistant Chief Constable Mark Dexter said: "GMP detectives and staff have been working on this investigation throughout the last 48 hours to ensure charges are brought in this case "Criminal proceedings must now take its course without interference."

Dani Bekyarova-Delev, of Stockport, Greater Manchester, said she was confident the designer item, bought in 2024, was genuine because she had used the platform's authentication service. Depop, eBay as well as Vinted have previously said they would suspend or ban users if they are caught selling counterfeit goods. title: Blaze breaks out at Trafford suspected illegal waste dump

evidence_packet.title: Blaze breaks out at Trafford suspected illegal waste dump
evidence_packet.lead: A fire broke out at a suspected illegal waste site near Carrington Spur in Trafford, Greater Manchester
evidence_packet.summary: A fire broke out at a suspected illegal waste site near Carrington Spur in Trafford, Greater Manchester
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Blaze breaks out at Trafford suspected illegal waste dump - BBC News Image caption, Fire crews wearing breathing apparatus tackled the blaze close to the River Mersey near the Carrington Spur By Richard Stead North West Published 10 August 2026 Firefighters have been tackling a blaze at a suspected illegal waste dump close to the River Mersey in Greater Manchester. Crews were called to the scene at 11:30 BST on Monday after reports that smoke had been coming from the site in woodland close to the Carrington Spur. Helen Carr from Flixton, who walks her dogs in woodland nearby, said: "The smell is absolutely acrid and what I really worry about is things like builders' waste setting on fire, then releasing all sorts of chemicals into the air. "Its criminal. There is just no need for people to be dumping waste like this, in this day and age. This is just sheer greed and laziness." Image caption, Helen Carr said she was concerned about the waste being dumped at the site The 43 year-old added: "The type of rubbish being dumped used to be agricultural waste, but it now involves builders waste alongside household waste, with things like mattresses and fridge freezers. "The waste has just being growing and growing and getting out of control." In July, Ms Carr reported the waste to the Environment Agency (EA), which responded by saying they were aware of the site and has referred the case to the Area Enforcement Team. In an email to Ms Carr, the EA said: "We take illegal waste offences seriously and will use the powers available to us to investigate and, where appropriate, take enforcement action against those responsible." evidence_packet.title: New funding to 'restore pride' in Greater Manchester high streets

evidence_packet.summary: Mayor Bev Craig said interested parties can apply for a share of the £20m pot later this year
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Businesses, charities and community groups across Greater Manchester will soon be able to apply for a share of a new £20m fund aimed at improving local high streets Mayor Bev Craig announced the Good Growth High Streets Fund during a visit to Middleton town centre, saying she wanted people to feel the benefits of Greater Manchester's economic growth in the places where they live The fund is expected to open for applications later this year, although details of how much individual projects will be able to bid for have not yet been announced The mayor's office says the scheme could support a range of ideas to help town and district centres attract more visitors, including bringing empty shops back into use and supporting community events Craig said many residents were concerned by the decline of some high streets, pointing to boarded-up shops, derelict buildings and the loss of independent businesses "Our high streets are the beating hearts of our communities, and people want to feel pride about where they live," she said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Buried abuse memory brought sisters' half-brother to justice - BBC News Image source, Family photo Image caption, Nikita Dallison and Mellissa Arkwright have waived their right to anonymity to share what happened to them By Lauren Hirst North West Published 10 August 2026 Sisters Nikita Dallison and Mellissa Arkwright were just six and seven years old when they began to be abused by their half-brother Adrian Austin. But while Nikita, 36, can remember the harrowing details vividly, Mellissa, 35, had no recollection of what happened to her as a little girl. It was only when Nikita bravely reported the abuse to police in 2021 that Mellissa decided to have a type of talking therapy known as eye movement desensitisation and reprocessing (EMDR). This involves listening to sounds, tapping, or flashing lights to remember a traumatic event. "I needed therapy because my mental health had spiralled way out of control... but I never understood why," said Mellissa. "It's horrific when you have it, because you feel every single sensation. "You can feel the atmosphere in the room when you're having that therapy." It unlocked a specific memory that would prove to be a crucial part of the evidence that brought their half-brother to justice. Austin, now aged 45, was jailed for 17 years in July after being found guilty of six counts of sexual intercourse with a girl under 13, which would be classed as rape under current sexual offences legislation. He was also convicted of four counts of indecent assault and one count of indecency of a child between 1997 and 2001. title: Solar eclipse: Where and when you can see it across North-West England

evidence_packet.title: Solar eclipse: Where and when you can see it across North-West England
evidence_packet.lead: The partial eclipse is expected to be the most extensive since 1999, astronomers say
evidence_packet.summary: The partial eclipse is expected to be the most extensive since 1999, astronomers say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The most dramatic partial solar eclipse of the century will be visible across the UK this week Astronomers say between 90% and 96% of the sun will slowly disappear behind the moon on the evening of Wednesday 12 August While the people of Greenland, Iceland and parts of northern Spain will be lucky enough to see a total eclipse, it will still represent the highest level of coverage seen from the UK since 11 August 1999 With Wednesday's event also calculated to be the most extensive solar eclipse for the next 54 years, it is clear why astronomers are calling it "really exciting" Experts say that while the sky will not fall into total darkness, the partial eclipse will be enough to make a "noticeable difference" in temperature and light levels According to the Royal Greenwich Observatory, times will vary slightly across the UK

title: Conflict ruling hits plans for Greater Manchester's tallest tower

evidence_packet.title: Conflict ruling hits plans for Greater Manchester's tallest tower
evidence_packet.lead: The development, which would reshape skyline with a 78-storey skyscraper, must return to a planning panel
evidence_packet.summary: The development, which would reshape skyline with a 78-storey skyscraper, must return to a planning panel
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plans to build Greater Manchester's tallest tower have suffered a setback after a planning approval process was ruled to have been affected by a conflict of interest Henley Investment Management secured approval last November for plans to partly demolish Regent Retail Park and build about 3,300 homes across 10 buildings. The development would include a 78-storey skyscraper, making it the tallest building in the region The scheme was approved despite opposition from more than 460 residents, who raised concerns about over-development and pressure on local infrastructure Objections were also lodged by Salford MP Rebecca Long-Bailey and several current and former councillors However, the approval process is now set to be reconsidered after a complaint by the Save Regent Retail Park campaign group was upheld by Salford City Council's legal department The complaint found there had been a "procedural conflict of interest" involving councillor Philip Cusack, then chair of the planning committee, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said it was "extremely grateful" for the group's help
evidence_packet.summary: Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said it was "extremely grateful" for the group's help
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A gamekeeper has said he "knew he had to do his bit" and help try and put out the moorland fires which have burnt above Greater Manchester Jono Simmonds, 37, who works as a gamekeeper on the Stalybridge Estate was one of about 20 others from surrounding areas who have been working around the clock to get on top of the fires, alongside Greater Manchester Fire Service, who have thanked the men for their work "We knew we had to do our bit to stop it and fortunately a lot of the lads jumped on and were here to help," Jono said Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said it was "extremely grateful" for the contribution of those who know and work on the land "When you're facing it and thinking it's all going to go up in smoke, it's heartbreaking," Jono added Earlier this week, Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service said a "stand down" decision had been taken after a review on Monday

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Plans to build Greater Manchester's tallest tower have suffered a setback after a planning approval process was ruled to have been affected by a conflict of interest Henley Investment Management secured approval last November for plans to partly demolish Regent Retail Park and build about 3,300 homes across 10 buildings. The development would include a 78-storey skyscraper, making it the tallest building in the region The scheme was approved despite opposition from more than 460 residents, who raised concerns about over-development and pressure on local infrastructure Objections were also lodged by Salford MP Rebecca Long-Bailey and several current and former councillors However, the approval process is now set to be reconsidered after a complaint by the Save Regent Retail Park campaign group was upheld by Salford City Council's legal department The complaint found there had been a "procedural conflict of interest" involving councillor Philip Cusack, then chair of the planning committee, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Rich-kid conman who fleeced clients over 'money-can't buy' handbags has appeal thrown out Fantasist Jack Watkins dubbed himself the 'Kardashian of Cheshire' News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 17:56, 10 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Jack Watkins' gained h A conman who fleeced clients out of tens of thousands of pounds in a luxury handbag scam has had an appeal against his prison sentence thrown out Fantasist Jack Watkin , an influencer who styled himself the 'Kardashian of Cheshire' , was jailed last year for a string of frauds. The privately-educated 26-year-old used his charm and life of privilege to defraud a string of victims in what detectives described as the 'frenzie A court heard how the victims were told by Watkin that he had contacts that could give them access to the handbags and that they could split the profits made on resale. But after handing over their money, there was no bag or sign of investment opportunities Last year Watkin, formerly of Wilmslow Road, Alderley Edge, was jailed for four and a half year after he pleaded guilty to six counts of fraud after duping unsuspecting victims, who included a close friend and his father, into handing over almost £200,000. A jury at Chester Crown He spent his money in Harrods and staying in five-star London hotel The Dorchester, where he ran up a bill of more than £100,000, police said. He was also jailed for another 18 months after being found guilty of several charges of possession of indecent images

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The question is do they care? They know deep down that land is greenbelt' A 192-acre stretch of green belt between Astley and Boothstown could be opened up for homes, business space and leisure development as Wigan Council seeks to meet its housing a Comments News Neal Keeling Chief reporter 05:58, 11 Aug 2026 Updated 06:27, 11 Aug 2026 Just a quarter of a mile from the East Lancs Road I walk across fields and through woods. We pass horses grazing, scorched acres providing early hay, and the air is brimming with birdsong Children are cavorting on a playground, and dog walkers zig-zag across the land. In the shadow of the lattice headgear of the former Astley pit this is most definitely green belt Leaning over one fence next to a watering trough for horses there is a huge expanse of hedgerows and fields with Boothstown in the distance I am with Joanna Allsop, a high school teacher who has lived in Astley, Wigan, all her life. We are in the tiny village of Astley Green on Higher Green Lane. It is a cluster of cottages, and terraced homes, and is served by the Old Boat House pub next to the Bridgewater Canal The road beyond the pub and over the canal leads to Astley Moss and ultimately a maze of farm tracks and roads to Chat Moss and Irlam

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police Student police officer, 23, charged with rape and kidnapping offences while off-duty Mohammad Hassan has been remanded in custody News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 22:33, 10 Aug 2026 View Image (Image: Manchester Evening New Greater Manchester Police has charged one of its student police officers with multiple offences following a police pursuit on the M62 on Saturday night (August 8) Mohammed Hassan, aged 23, who is understood to have been an officer-in-training, has been charged with oral rape, kidnap, strangulation and sexual assault He has also been charged with dangerous driving and theft of a mobile phone. The definition of a vape shop will also be tightened to stop businesses getting around the new rules by cla The Government also intends to revoke the Gambling Act's ‘Aim to Permit’ rule, which currently restricts the ability of councils to refuse new betting shops and 24-hour slot machine shops. title: Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant

evidence_packet.title: Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant "He is just the epitome of sunshine.
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant "He is just the epitome of sunshine. I can’t even put into words how great he is." Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 20:26 A 38-year-old father of two
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant "He is just the epitome of sunshine. I can’t even put into words how great he is." Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 20:26 A 38-year-old father of two who suffered a heart attack after starting his shift at Manchester Airport is now urgently waiting for a heart transplant Jamie Maclean, known as Jambo by his colleagues, collapsed three weeks ago at his job at STS Aviation Services early on a Tuesday morning and was taken to Wythenshawe Hospital After a stent wasn't successful, Jamie flatlined and had to be resuscitated. Due to fluid in his lungs, the 38-year-old developed pneumonia and, as a result, his heart, kidneys, and liver began to fail Doctors placed him in an induced coma, which he came out of on Friday (August 7). Once awake, he decided to opt for a full heart transplant because 'nothing was working' and he 'just wants his independence back' View 3 Images Jamie with his two teenage sons (Image: Jamie Maclean)

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Couple lost nearly £1,000 after confusing rule scuppered dream holiday at Manchester Airport Peter Wiles and his wife Rogelyn Caresosa had been planning to go on a holiday to Cappadocia in Turkey, but their holiday ended at Manchest Peter and Rogelyn Wiles had been looking forward to a romantic getaway in Cappadocia, a region of Turkey famous for its colourful hot air balloons and underground cities carved out of soft volcanic ash. The couple married in 2024, paving the way for Rogelyn to move to the UK on a And having saved up the cash for the May 2025 getaway, Peter splashed out £973.30 for flights from Manchester Airport. But the couple, from Crewe, were left distraught - and out of pocket - when their dream getaway ended at the airport "My wife was devastated, we had to get a taxi home as it was late on a Sunday and the trains had finished," Peter said. "This whole debacle has honestly had me questioning my sanity at times!" Peter had booked and paid for the flights for himself and his Filipino wife, as part of a single booking in his name, using his Tesco Bank credit card But because Rogelyn holds a UK spouse visa, her old Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) card had technically expired at the end of 2024 under the UK's switch to digital eVisas, although her actual immigration status remains valid until 2027

Works to the children’s play area, the café and both the wa Pets corner will also be revamped, while the footprint of the former Longford Hall will also be ‘reinterpreted to celebrate the site's history’ and Long Barn will be turned into a volunteer, training and skills hub. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Hundreds of illegal goods seized as ‘dodgy shop’ crackdown begins in Bury This is 'only the beginning', the town hall has promised Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:40, 10 Aug 2026 View Image Grace the sniffer dog and seized goods from Bury shop Hundreds of illegal goods have been seized from Bury shops as town hall bosses look to crackdown on ‘dodgy shops’ Among the illicit items discovered by Bury council trading officers were 397 packets of cigarettes, 51 pouches of hand-rolling tobacco, and 127 vapes from four shops in the borough. Counterfeit and potentially ‘unsafe’ children’s toys were taken from a fifth The local authority said the value of the goods, found with the assistance of Greater Manchester Police and Wagtail sniffer dog Grace, is thought to be around £8,500. The raid followed a recent promise by councillors to crackdown on the ‘scourge’ of so-called ‘dodgy shops’ embedd According to local leaders, these are shops deliberately trading outside the law while masquerading as legitimate businesses, and can be ‘gateways’ or drug dealing, money laundering, modern slavery, human trafficking and cybercrime Up to 50 per cent of mini-marts and vape shops - and up to a third of American candy shops - are believed to be ‘operating outside the law’, Labour councillor Michael Rubinstein told the chamber in July

evidence_packet.summary: But as our chief reporter Neal Keeling explains, 22 years on, the Whitefield heist remains unsolved Hundreds of tram passengers ride by it every day. It sits at the top of the hill as you look up from the Bury -bound platform at Whitefield Metrolink
evidence_packet.evidence_text: But as our chief reporter Neal Keeling explains, 22 years on, the Whitefield heist remains unsolved Hundreds of tram passengers ride by it every day. It sits at the top of the hill as you look up from the Bury -bound platform at Whitefield Metrolink . It is now 8 Whitefield, a Chinese restaurant on Bury New Road But 22 years ago it was the scene of one of the region's most infamous heists. Built from limestone with a domed corner in the 1930s in the All Saints Conservation Area the landmark was once a bank. In 2004 it was run by the NatWest View 5 Images The former NatWest bank in Whitefield was the scene for an infamous and unsolved robbery in 2004 (Image: Manchester Evening News) It was the target for a robbery that was so well planned and carried out with such precision and ruthlessness it was likened to a paramilitary operation. On September 21 that year at 8pm, two armed men wearing masks, wigs, and false beards, arrived at the family home of the bank' They held him and his wife, Lynne and two young daughters hostage. The two intruders communicated via a walkie-talkie with a third person called "Andy"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bramhall People in Bramhall say they are being 'picked on again' as bins will go unemptied for eight weeks The move has been labelled unfair and unacceptable but Stockport council said they 'remain focused on delivering a safe and reliable service for People in a Stockport village paying ‘some of the highest levels of council tax in the country’ will have to wait more than a month for their bins to be collected. The move has been labelled unfair and unacceptable Across Bramhall in Stockport , a number of residents have not had their blue bins because Stockport council-owned company Totally Local Company deemed them to be too full and left open . Blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling in Stockport are collected every four weeks This means their next scheduled collection will not take place until August 27, eight weeks after their bin was last collected on July 2 When people have approached the council to report the missed collection too , they have been told this is not possible because the bin crews reported the bin lid as ‘open’. Bramhall councillor Peter Crossen said the situation was unacceptable and he is ‘extremely unhappy that it’ View 3 Images Uncollected bins in Bramhall which Stockport Council did not collect because the lid was 'open'. Have your say Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers, who were jailed for manslaughter, will be freed in January under existing plans Comments News Ashlie Blakey Live and br Andy Burnham has asked his Justice Secretary to 'work through further options' to prevent the early release of PC Andrew Harper’s killers The Prime Minister is facing increasing pressure from PC Harper's family and the police not to allow Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers to be freed in January under existing plans. The pair were sentenced to 13 years for manslaughter in 2020 PC Harper was fatally injured when he got caught in a strap attached to the back of a car and was dragged down a country road as the killers fled the scene of a quad bike theft in Sulhamstead, Berkshire, in 2019. Two out of three of his killers, Cole and Bowers, are set to be rel Around 5,000 people are expected to be released early under sentencing changes, down from 6,000 after some exemptions were announced as part of an urgent review of the scheme to tackle jail overcrowding. Exemptions were made for those convicted of rape, serious child sex offences On Monday, Downing Street said it was 'not possible' to exempt 'one or two offenders' convicted of manslaughter from the early release scheme. However, Justice Secretary Alex Norris will now look at ways to keep 'a greater number of the the most serious offenders' behind bars

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Ardwick Crying children, dirty toilets and poor teaching - the Manchester nursery which requires 'urgent improvement' Ardwick Day Nursey has been criticised by Ofsted Comments News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 06:39, 11 Aug 2026 View Image Ardwick day Nur A Manchester nursery has been ordered to make drastic improvements after Ofsted uncovered a catalogue of failings Inspectors found children at Ardwick Day Nursery cried for 'prolonged periods of time' because they felt unsettled and the toilets and nappy changing areas were unhygienic because they are not cleaned regularly. Teaching at the Hyde Road nursery was said to be 'poor', while the w "Children with SEND struggle to settle, regularly become frustrated and have not developed secure bonds with a trusted adult," a report said. "This significantly undermines their emotional wellbeing and prevents them from being ready to learn." Frequent staffing changes mean children fail to form relationships with staff, while a poorly implemented curriculum means they 'do not achieve well', Ofsted said "Children do not develop the essential knowledge and skills that they need for their future success," the report said. "They are not adequately prepared to move on to the next stage of learning, including moving on to school."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester Airport worker suffers sudden heart attack and is put into coma - now needs heart transplant "He is just the epitome of sunshine. I can’t even put into words how great he is." Comments News Charlotte Fisher Reporter 20:26 A 38-year-old father of two who suffered a heart attack after starting his shift at Manchester Airport is now urgently waiting for a heart transplant Jamie Maclean, known as Jambo by his colleagues, collapsed three weeks ago at his job at STS Aviation Services early on a Tuesday morning and was taken to Wythenshawe Hospital After a stent wasn't successful, Jamie flatlined and had to be resuscitated. Due to fluid in his lungs, the 38-year-old developed pneumonia and, as a result, his heart, kidneys, and liver began to fail Doctors placed him in an induced coma, which he came out of on Friday (August 7). evidence_packet.evidence_text: M62 M62 to close every night for six weeks as repairs take place on landmark bridge The closure to allow bridge repairs to take place has already been pushed back twice News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 19:52, 10 Aug 2026 View Image Repairs will be carrie The M62 will be closed every weeknight until the end of September for repairs to a landmark bridge Drivers are being warned the motorway will be shut in both directions overnight Monday to Friday, from August 17. It's to allow delayed repairs to Scammonden Bridge, just over the Greater Manchester border in West Yorkshire to take place The work was due to start in April, with the bridge closed through to October. But those plans were scrapped due to what National Highways described as 'customer feedback' A second start date of July 20 was also delayed due to the moor fires in Tintwistle which closed Woodhead Pass, one of the only other major routes from Greater Manchester to Yorkshire. Work will now begin next Monday with the M62 set to close from 8pm to 6am every weeknight Eastbound traffic will be diverted via A672, A58 , A646 , A629, while westbound traffic will be diverted via A629, A646, A58, A672. The bridge itself will remain closed weeknights until work is completed in January 2027

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Couple lost nearly £1,000 after confusing rule scuppered dream holiday at Manchester Airport Peter Wiles and his wife Rogelyn Caresosa had been planning to go on a holiday to Cappadocia in Turkey, but their holiday ended at Manchest Peter and Rogelyn Wiles had been looking forward to a romantic getaway in Cappadocia, a region of Turkey famous for its colourful hot air balloons and underground cities carved out of soft volcanic ash. The couple married in 2024, paving the way for Rogelyn to move to the UK on a And having saved up the cash for the May 2025 getaway, Peter splashed out £973.30 for flights from Manchester Airport. But the couple, from Crewe, were left distraught - and out of pocket - when their dream getaway ended at the airport "My wife was devastated, we had to get a taxi home as it was late on a Sunday and the trains had finished," Peter said. "This whole debacle has honestly had me questioning my sanity at times!" Peter had booked and paid for the flights for himself and his Filipino wife, as part of a single booking in his name, using his Tesco Bank credit card But because Rogelyn holds a UK spouse visa, her old Biometric Residence Permit (BRP) card had technically expired at the end of 2024 under the UK's switch to digital eVisas, although her actual immigration status remains valid until 2027

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Cheshire Rich-kid conman who fleeced clients over 'money-can't buy' handbags has appeal thrown out Fantasist Jack Watkins dubbed himself the 'Kardashian of Cheshire' News Damon Wilkinson Reporter 17:56, 10 Aug 2026 View 2 Images Jack Watkins' gained h A conman who fleeced clients out of tens of thousands of pounds in a luxury handbag scam has had an appeal against his prison sentence thrown out Fantasist Jack Watkin , an influencer who styled himself the 'Kardashian of Cheshire' , was jailed last year for a string of frauds. The privately-educated 26-year-old used his charm and life of privilege to defraud a string of victims in what detectives described as the 'frenzie A court heard how the victims were told by Watkin that he had contacts that could give them access to the handbags and that they could split the profits made on resale. But after handing over their money, there was no bag or sign of investment opportunities Last year Watkin, formerly of Wilmslow Road, Alderley Edge, was jailed for four and a half year after he pleaded guilty to six counts of fraud after duping unsuspecting victims, who included a close friend and his father, into handing over almost £200,000. A jury at Chester Crown He spent his money in Harrods and staying in five-star London hotel The Dorchester, where he ran up a bill of more than £100,000, police said. He was also jailed for another 18 months after being found guilty of several charges of possession of indecent images

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bury Hundreds of illegal goods seized as ‘dodgy shop’ crackdown begins in Bury This is 'only the beginning', the town hall has promised Comments News Hannah Richardson 17:40, 10 Aug 2026 View Image Grace the sniffer dog and seized goods from Bury shop Hundreds of illegal goods have been seized from Bury shops as town hall bosses look to crackdown on ‘dodgy shops’ Among the illicit items discovered by Bury council trading officers were 397 packets of cigarettes, 51 pouches of hand-rolling tobacco, and 127 vapes from four shops in the borough. Counterfeit and potentially ‘unsafe’ children’s toys were taken from a fifth The local authority said the value of the goods, found with the assistance of Greater Manchester Police and Wagtail sniffer dog Grace, is thought to be around £8,500. The raid followed a recent promise by councillors to crackdown on the ‘scourge’ of so-called ‘dodgy shops’ embedd According to local leaders, these are shops deliberately trading outside the law while masquerading as legitimate businesses, and can be ‘gateways’ or drug dealing, money laundering, modern slavery, human trafficking and cybercrime Up to 50 per cent of mini-marts and vape shops - and up to a third of American candy shops - are believed to be ‘operating outside the law’, Labour councillor Michael Rubinstein told the chamber in July

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Update on ‘exciting’ £6m transformation of ‘best-loved’ Trafford park The council wants to ‘create a better park for all ages and abilities to enjoy’ Comments News Hannah Richardson 16:52, 10 Aug 2026 View 2 Images CGI image of the planned Lo Work to transform a Trafford park can now get underway after contracts were finalised, the town hall has said Longford Park, in Stretford , is set for a £6m improvement scheme that is expected to include a new BMX track, improvements to the tennis and basketball courts and football pitches, and upgrades to cricket and disc golf. Works to the children’s play area, the café and both the wa Pets corner will also be revamped, while the footprint of the former Longford Hall will also be ‘reinterpreted to celebrate the site's history’ and Long Barn will be turned into a volunteer, training and skills hub. Work is expected to get underway this month, Trafford council do The authority said Longford Park is one of its oldest and “best-loved parks”. The scheme has previously been touted as a “project of borough-wide significance”, with the Labour administration saying it “complements” the transformation of Stretford town centre Town hall bosses hope the plan will ‘create a better park for all ages and abilities to enjoy’. Some closure are expected to be needed during the works, but the authority said it will do its ‘best’ to ‘minimise disruption’ and ‘keep as many facilities open as possible’

evidence_packet.evidence_text: But as our chief reporter Neal Keeling explains, 22 years on, the Whitefield heist remains unsolved Hundreds of tram passengers ride by it every day. It sits at the top of the hill as you look up from the Bury -bound platform at Whitefield Metrolink . It is now 8 Whitefield, a Chinese restaurant on Bury New Road But 22 years ago it was the scene of one of the region's most infamous heists. Built from limestone with a domed corner in the 1930s in the All Saints Conservation Area the landmark was once a bank. In 2004 it was run by the NatWest View 5 Images The former NatWest bank in Whitefield was the scene for an infamous and unsolved robbery in 2004 (Image: Manchester Evening News) It was the target for a robbery that was so well planned and carried out with such precision and ruthlessness it was likened to a paramilitary operation. On September 21 that year at 8pm, two armed men wearing masks, wigs, and false beards, arrived at the family home of the bank' They held him and his wife, Lynne and two young daughters hostage. The two intruders communicated via a walkie-talkie with a third person called "Andy"

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bramhall People in Bramhall say they are being 'picked on again' as bins will go unemptied for eight weeks The move has been labelled unfair and unacceptable but Stockport council said they 'remain focused on delivering a safe and reliable service for People in a Stockport village paying ‘some of the highest levels of council tax in the country’ will have to wait more than a month for their bins to be collected. The move has been labelled unfair and unacceptable Across Bramhall in Stockport , a number of residents have not had their blue bins because Stockport council-owned company Totally Local Company deemed them to be too full and left open . Blue bins for paper and cardboard recycling in Stockport are collected every four weeks This means their next scheduled collection will not take place until August 27, eight weeks after their bin was last collected on July 2 When people have approached the council to report the missed collection too , they have been told this is not possible because the bin crews reported the bin lid as ‘open’. Bramhall councillor Peter Crossen said the situation was unacceptable and he is ‘extremely unhappy that it’ View 3 Images Uncollected bins in Bramhall which Stockport Council did not collect because the lid was 'open'. evidence_packet.evidence_text: on WhatsApp Share via Email Trafford Council's children's services have been rated inadequate in two key areas by Ofsted, with inspectors warning that delays in responding to concerns about children have left some at risk of harm The report, published yesterday following a two-week inspection between June 8th and 19th, judged both the impact of leaders on social work practice and the experiences of children who need help and protection to be inadequate - the watchdog's lowest grade Services for children in care were rated good, while support for care leavers requires improvement to be good Inspectors, led by His Majesty's Inspector Leanne Cooper, found that since the council's last full inspection in 2022 - when it was rated requires improvement across the board - leaders had failed to recognise and act on shortfalls in critical parts of the service The sharpest criticism was reserved for the council's "front door" - the point at which concerns about children are first reported. The report found that responses to contacts about children take too long, are not prioritised in line with risk, and that many children face lengthy Strategy discussions - urgent multi-agency meetings held when a child is identified as being at risk of significant harm - are too often delayed, leaving children in potentially unsafe situations for too long and at risk of what inspectors called unassessed significant harm

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Council is reminding residents to recycle electrical items responsibly this summer due to dangers posed to waste collection crews As temperatures rise and the use of electrical items such as fans, portable chargers, and other rechargeable items increase, the council is urging residents to ensure unwanted electricals are taken to the correct recycling facilities Research from Material Focus has highlighted the growing popularity of low-cost electrical products, often known as ‘FastTech’, which can be easily forgotten, thrown away, or incorrectly disposed of. Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

Cost: £150 for the full course. Bursaries are available for those on lower income – please email learning@bandonthewall.org to arrange this.. . Spaces are limited – Book here . . . In this show Mike talks about doing psychedelics with his brother, an entanglement with a Spanish Sausage Dog named Nino, and many other such rotten adventures ‘ Ireland has yet another legendary comedian ‘ – Dan Nightingale Irish farmer’s son, and general Nasty Character Mike Rice is one of Ireland and the UK’s fastest rising comedy stars. Having started comedy in 2016 Mike has amassed a large online following from podcast and stand-up clips, regularly getting millions of views on various platforms Mike began stand-up comedy in Chicago, where within two years he was working regularly at the most prestigious clubs in the city, including The Laugh Factory. He has since returned home because his mother made him, and has been quickly rising in the Irish and European scene, play Mike brought his first solo show The Best Boy in Ireland to the Edinburgh Fringe Festival 2018, in what was a sold-out run, and performed that same show to sold-out rooms at the Perth Fringe Festival in 2019 As well as co-hosting Mike & Vittorio’s Guide to Parenting with Vittorio Angelone, and Big Mike and The Chief with Rob Moriarty, Mike has appeared multiple times on smash hit podcast Have a Word and released his first comedy special in October 2023
